correctness.rationale: A fixed-coordinate subset is completable exactly when it is independent in its new-stratum collision graph. Since each new stratum has width less than each old stratum, each coordinate contributes a matching. Componentwise maximum independent sets provide the exact O(n) optimum. Independent Bernoulli shifts produce adjacent 1-to-0 collisions, exact full-retention probability, and 1/6 collision density per axis. Uniform coordinate permutation converts the union into two independent partial matchings conditional on sizes. Alternating paths have geometrically decaying length tails at incidence p=1/3; finite neighborhood and two-root limits give odd-path density p(1-p)/(2(1+p)) for each colour. The exact matching-number identity gives deletion p/(1+p)=1/4. Checker passed 46,948 deterministic/exact assertions and a separately labeled simulation tolerance; finite checks are not used to infer infinite limits.

value.rationale: Fixed-point preservation is motivated by avoiding re-evaluation of expensive experiments after increasing a two-dimensional Latin-hypercube design. A generic exponential-time maximum-independent-set method is replaced by an exact linear-time procedure using two coordinate orders. For randomly jittered designs, the new target size n+1 requires discarding about n/4 old evaluations even under optimal retention, while no-change preservation is exponentially rare with a specified exact formula. These are substantive computational and design-cost statements about the motivating natural extension objective.
